question: I mean the order in which you do your jobs. What difference does having a usual sequence make, if any?
model_evidence: model and effort in native CLI rollout turn_context record
raw: “Oh, yes—a usual order means I’m not stopping to work out what comes next each time. Wash the bibs, get them into the bag, put it by the door. I can follow that along. If I break off halfway, I sometimes have to look through the bag again to see what I’ve actually done. The washing’s done, but have I packed them? That sort of thing. Having the same order helps me keep my place.”
